Cyber Attack Disrupts Ukraine’s Transportation and Logistics Firms

KYIV, Ukraine, June 14 – A major cyber attack targeting Ukraine’s transportation and logistics industry has disrupted freight operations and caused widespread delays, industry officials and government sources said Friday. The incident, which began late Thursday and was ongoing at the time of reporting, involved ransomware affecting the IT systems of several leading logistics firms.

According to Ukraine’s Ministry of Infrastructure, the attack has primarily affected cargo tracking systems and scheduling platforms, hampering the movement of goods by rail and truck across multiple regions. The ministry said it was coordinating efforts with affected companies and the State Cyber Protection Center to contain the breach, but warned that services could remain disrupted for at least another 48 hours.

“Preliminary analysis indicates that the attackers gained access to internal networks and encrypted key operational data,” said Kateryna Bondarenko, spokesperson for the ministry. “This has resulted in significant delays at key transit hubs and border crossings. Our teams are working around the clock to restore normal operations.”

Among the firms impacted is Dnipro Freight Solutions, whose CEO, Oleg Marchenko, described the situation as “critical” in a statement to local media. “We are unable to process new shipments or provide real-time tracking information to our clients. Our IT staff are cooperating with law enforcement and cybersecurity experts in an effort to recover encrypted files,” Marchenko said.

The Ukrainian Association of Road Carriers reported that the attack has led to a backlog of more than 1,000 trucks at the Yagodyn and Chop border crossings with Poland and Hungary, respectively. “Drivers are experiencing wait times of up to 18 hours, with perishable goods at particular risk,” said association president Serhiy Kravets. He added that some firms have suspended cross-border shipments until systems are restored.

Industry analysts warn that the attack comes at a particularly sensitive time, as Ukraine’s transportation and logistics sector is handling increased demand for both imports and humanitarian aid. “Even a 24-hour disruption can have cascading effects on supply chains, especially for time-sensitive deliveries,” said Viktoria Ishchenko, a Kyiv-based logistics consultant.

The State Cyber Protection Center has not yet attributed the attack to any group but said in a statement that it bore hallmarks of previous ransomware incidents targeting critical infrastructure. Authorities have urged firms in the sector to review their cyber defenses and report any suspicious activity.

As of Friday afternoon, technical teams were attempting to restore access to compromised systems and bypass locked files. “We urge patience from our partners and customers as we work to resolve this unprecedented challenge,” said Bondarenko.
